I'm totally blind and I've been that way since birth: AMA.
What types of technologies do you use in your daily life?
I use 2 systems with win 7. I also use an iPhone 6. When it comes to screen readers, I use both JAWS and NVDA.
Have you ever thought about trying to use that 'clicking' echo location technique and if so, are you daredevil?

Did you just ask me if I can fly? No I haven't really tried the technique, although I can explain how it works. It works by the way the air bounces off buildings. You don't necissarily have to use the clicking to hear air bouncing off buildings, you can just hear it.

I didn't have a chance to watch your entire video but I did browse through it a bit. It was really interesting to see/hear the technology you use for your phone and the internet. You also seem to have a very nice and cheerful way about you.

What are some of your hobbies and general interests?

Yeah, that video is long, sorry about that! Well, I'm an avid web surfer! Thus the username. Besides that, I have an interest in airplanes and flying, mostly because I'd like to learn someday. I actually did fly a plane once, (with someone else teaching me how to use the stick and such, of course,) and I'd like to take a lesson or 2. I like to follow flying and space flight. I also like to sing, that doesn't mean I'm a good singer, and I don't do it in public, (besides in church,) because I've been told not to. I also enjoy dancing, I took ballet when I was in 9th-11th grade.

How do you conceptualize a camera? I see you talking about turning the camera around on your phone, so you clearly understand it as a way for people to know where you are in space without touching you. Still, without any firsthand concept of sight, does it seem like black magic that pointing a plastic thing at yourself allows people far away to "feel" the landscape of the room you're in?

I know where the back camera is on my phone, because there's actually an indentation there.) The thing is, is when I try to flip it, the Meerkat app has this weird bug where it takes me completely out of the app, which stops the stream. When I flip around and use the front camera, I just turn the phone and point the screen at my face, (holding it vertically.)
Lol I think it's hilarious that someone downvoted this thread! Apparently they didn't think I should let people ask me questions?

How do you feel about being blind? How often do you find yourself thinking about it?

And what's one interesting thing most people wouldn't know about being blind and the lifestyle associated with it? :)

I don't think about it often. I guess it's just something I'm used to. In other words, there are more important things going on in the world, and I have more important things to deal with right now, (moving, for instance.) Well, I can tell you an interesting thing about me, (and I know a blind friend of mine says he does the same thing.) I talk to myself, ( a lot .) I think in words, out loud.
Wow that's super cool. Thanks for doing this AMA! Do you spend a lot of time online or is it too much of a hassle? What do you spend most of your time doing?
Lol, I spend all my time online, except for when I'm at church.
Oh wow! Well if you're ever bored we'd love to have you in our irc channel also :)
IRC isn't something I've ever done, I'm afraid it would be waaaayyyy too fast for the screen reader, and then I'd end up getting behind.
I'd like to try IRC, I just need a very slow channel to try it in.
I'm very proficient at the Twitterz though!
Asking the hard questions here, how do you know when you're done wiping?
What is it like falling asleep? Do you have trouble staying awake during the day?

Trouble staying awake during the day? Not usually, unless I have a really bad headache. I get headaches often, which make me tired. I do take Benadryl and Melatonin for sleep, as I was on some antidepressants that caused insomnia and was just able to come off those last month. I didn't actually need the antidepressnats, (it's a long story about 2 doctors getting things mixed up and others in the mix when they shouldn't have been.)The doctor's told me not to take any sleep aids, (except the natural melatonin,) and the antihistamine Benadryl.) I also don't usually wake up at night unless I have to use the bathroom, or I'm extremely thirsty, (which tends to happen,) and then I fall right back to sleep. Falling asleep is like well... I don't know how to describe it, I'm awake until I'm not anymore I guess.
Are there times that you catch yourself forgetting that you are blind? If so please expand.

No, that's never happened to me. However, I've had that happen with other people, especially if they're first getting to know me. They just assume that when they're handing me something, I'm looking at where their hand is, and then they're like "oh, I forgot..." This usually comes after the usual "ya know, I'm blind, this means I can't see anything at all," introduction.

What do you do when you need to memorize something? Is there any way you can write in Braille or do you just use a sound recorder? For example, how did you learn the multiplication tables? How would you learn the capitals of the world?

I used to read braille when I was in school. Not anymore though, (it takes too long, and I can't retain what I read.) If I really need to memorize something, (as I do to deliver occasional speeches,) I type it out in the computer first, and I rehearse it. I do this by having the screen reader read it, and then reciting what the screen reader says. I'm actually very good at remembering some things, I don't use an email address book for instance. For phone numbers, I just put them into my iPhone's contacts, and I use Siri to call and/or text each person.
Do you ever have trouble keeping a sleep schedule?

No, not usually. The only time I've ever had trouble with that are before I used to do my 24 hour blogging events for charity... my body used to play tricks on me! Also, I was put on antidepressants recently that did cause me insomnia, I was taken off of them. So no, except for one month out of the year.
